newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Opposition capture Taleban-held town in north.
newsitem.headline: Opposition capture Taleban-held town in north.

text.p: Pul-i-Khumri, the last major Taleban-held town in northeastern Afghanistan, fell to opposition forces on Wednesday, witnesses said.
They said opposition forces moved into Pul-i-Khumri, south of Mazar-i-Sharif, about 4 a.m. (2330 GMT Tuesday) after the purist Islamic militia evacuated northwards toward the town of Baghlan.

"Last night at about 11 p.m. (1830 GMT), we launched an attack and pushed them back. They attacked back, but could not hold us. We entered the city at about 4:15 a.m. (2345 GMT Tuesday)," said Sayed Jafar Naderi, an opposition commander.
The Taleban held the town of Pul-i-Khumri for two weeks. They captured it after a column of their forces crossed the Hindu Kush mountain range north of Kabul.

Shortly after they crossed the mountains, the road was closed as opposition forces attacked and captured the town of Jabal-os-Siraj, the southern gateway to the Salang Pass, leaving the Taleban garrision in Pul-i-Khumri surrounded.
Naderi told reporters he believed many of the stranded Taleban fighters had fled north towards Baghlan, but said he expected Baghlan residents to disarm them and hand them over.
